body:
Safety in a sport organisation refers to the structures, policies, practices, and culture that protect people from harm while enabling sport to be delivered effectively. It covers the full operating environment of the organisation, including facilities, programmes, events, staff, volunteers, athletes, participants, spectators, contractors, and community stakeholders.

A sport organisation has a duty to ensure that safety is planned, managed, communicated, and continuously improved. This means identifying risks before activities take place, putting in place appropriate controls, preparing for emergencies, and learning from incidents when they occur.

Safety should be embedded into everyday decision-making rather than treated as a separate compliance exercise.
The overarching policy connecting SportSG's individual safety policies into one coherent framework.
Sets the baseline safety standards expected across all SportSG-supported sport activity.
Covers safeguarding, athlete welfare, and protection from abuse or harassment in sport.
SportSG's Workplace Safety and Health obligations for staff, contractors, and facility operators.
Safety decisions flow from SportSG's Board through the Safety Governance function to operational teams and facility-level Safety Officers, each with defined authority to act.
SportSG and its partners operate under Singapore's Workplace Safety and Health Act and related regulations, alongside sport-specific statutory requirements.
Everyone delivering or hosting sport activity — SportSG staff, coaches, event operators, and partners — shares a duty of care to participants, spectators, and each other.
